# Claims Processing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Claims Processing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; keep the workshop synthetic, unpublished and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded claims files, proposed case, policy and document sources, and the intended channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the claims case, policy-administration, document, SIU and Teams seams. The workshop needs no customer connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare adjuster, manager, SIU, operations and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; do not publish the workshop to share it. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Regulated decision ownership | Name the adjuster, SIU, legal, compliance and payment reviewers before replacing synthetic claims; keep real claimant data out of the workshop. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Claim-file preparation across intake, policy, document, SIU and adjudication systems. Adjusters rebuild files across separate systems, and automated scoring can be mistaken for a coverage or fraud decision.

Fill your baseline record:

| Claim type | Measurement period | Systems consulted | File rebuild effort | Scores misread as decisions | Decision owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree claims replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Claims operations owner | Approve claims-preparation scope, production seams and success measures; never treat synthetic amounts or scores as results. |
| Authorized adjusters and claims managers | Validate coverage, causation, documentation and exclusions, and own approval, denial, reserve and settlement. |
| SIU investigators | Investigate flagged indicators and determine findings; a score never proves fraud. |
| Legal, compliance, coverage and payment authorities | Approve regulated decisions, jurisdictional questions and any payment the agent must not make. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, add no tools and record the owned agent's Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any claims-data connection is approved. |
| Claims connection owners | Approve the case, policy, document, SIU and Teams seams with least-privilege references; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CLP-01 through CLP-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject reshoot-required frames and uncited answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route claim decisions to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Planned claims replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed.
- [ ] The claims owner records where adjusters rebuild files across intake, policy, document, SIU and adjudication systems.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/claims-processing/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved and recorded before any build starts.
- [ ] The customer approves the authenticated claims-staff audience and least-privilege scopes for claimant and policy data.
- [ ] The environment's data policies for knowledge sources, connectors, skills and channels are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/claims-processing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/claims-processing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/claims-processing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/claims-processing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Claims Processing Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_claims-processing-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_claims-processing-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_adjudication-review_02
9. Add skill: aibast_claim-intake_01
10. Add skill: aibast_fraud-flag_03
11. Add skill: aibast_settlement-recommendation_04
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass CLP-01: Claims Operations Leader
15. Pass CLP-02: Claims Adjuster
16. Pass CLP-03: SIU Investigator
17. Pass CLP-04: Claims Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CLP-01, CLP-02, CLP-03, CLP-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `ClaimsProcessingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search is removed and no tools exist.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full final response; an annotated image is only a learner checkpoint.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before accessing claimant, policy or SIU information. Request only the scopes necessary for approved claims sources. Restrict the claims audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 claims case data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 claims case data — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 claims case data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 claims case data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 claims case data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No; the score is an explainable indicator for SIU review, not proof. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or claim change succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Policy-administration system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

1. **Bind Policy-administration system — read:** Bind approved read-only policy lookups.

2. **Identity for Policy-administration system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Policy-administration system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Policy-administration system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve and pay nothing; show the nonbinding estimate and state that no approval or payment occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report it as absent; never fill the gap from general knowledge.

### Step 3-3. Integrate SharePoint or approved claims document repository

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint or approved claims document repository — read:** Add approved document knowledge with least-privilege access.

2. **Identity for SharePoint or approved claims document repository:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint or approved claims document repository:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint or approved claims document repository:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no denial; list the missing documents for the authorized adjuster. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or claim change succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate SIU case workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

1. **Bind SIU case workflow — read:** Expose read-only SIU status; referrals stay with investigators.

2. **Identity for SIU case workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SIU case workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SIU case workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No; the score is an explainable indicator for SIU review, not proof. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or claim change succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams adjuster approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams adjuster approvals — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any approval-request workflow behind authorized review (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams adjuster approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams adjuster approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams adjuster approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Approve and pay nothing; show the nonbinding estimate and state that no approval or payment occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, referral or claim change succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims connection owners

Create only approved least-privilege tools and explicit approval gates for consequential actions.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only approved least-privilege tools exist, with explicit approval gates for consequential actions.
- [ ] No live lookup, referral or claim change is claimed unless an approved tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run adapted evaluations under an approved authenticated test profile so the agent's tools and connections are fully testable.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The claims owner sets acceptance thresholds on customer data; synthetic amounts, scores and estimates are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked claims corpus | All four cases, CLP-01 through CLP-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Regulated decision boundary | Any fraud, coverage, approval, denial, reserve, settlement, payment, referral or record-change claim is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reuse only frames with a positive expected-state anchor; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved claims audience and channels are selected, and the agent is tested in Preview before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Claims operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Claims operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Pull before editing, push reviewed changes, then package the workspace with `pac copilot pack` for solution import.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review claims session transcripts, failed turns, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, misrouted claim files, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
